strings.app.name: SpektraLab
strings.menu.help: Menu: import, export, edit, view, Settings, About
strings.toolbar.displayHelp: The photograph is colour managed to: {0}. Settings › Display changes how.
strings.toolbar.displayWarning: Display colour management: {0} Click for Settings › Display.
strings.settings.title: Settings
strings.settings.languageCaption: Film, paper, camera and lens names stay in English, as do technical abbreviations. The change applies immediately — nothing needs restarting. This build ships English; a language file in the i18n folder beside the app appears here.
strings.settings.scaleCaption: Scales the whole interface — the editor, Settings and About. Windows applies it the next time SpektraLab starts; this session runs at {0} %.
strings.settings.scaleEnvironment: QT_SCALE_FACTOR is set in the environment, so it decides the scale; this setting applies once it is removed.
strings.settings.resetLayoutCaption: Rail widths, which rails are folded, the filmstrip and which sections are open, back to the drawing.
strings.settings.checkUpdatesReason: The update check asks GitHub for the newest macOS release; the Windows build is a development build with no releases to compare against yet.
strings.settings.display.title: Colour management
strings.settings.display.automaticNote: The profile Windows assigns to the monitor this window is on, followed when the window moves to another monitor. Under Auto Color Management or HDR, Windows manages the window itself and the canvas draws sRGB; the status below says so.
strings.settings.display.srgbNote: Treat the monitor as sRGB: an sRGB photograph is drawn unchanged. For a monitor set to its sRGB mode, or to compare with an application that does not manage colour.
strings.settings.display.customNote: An .icc or .icm file you choose instead of the one Windows assigns — a new calibration not yet installed, say. A profile Qt cannot draw to (CMYK, greyscale, LUT-only) falls back to sRGB with the reason below.
strings.settings.display.chooseHelp: Choose an .icc or .icm display profile; choosing one selects Custom profile
strings.settings.display.reloadHelp: Ask Windows for the monitor's profile now
strings.settings.display.reloadNote: Windows announces no profile change. SpektraLab asks again when the window changes screen, on display and setting changes, when it becomes the active app, every 3 seconds, and when you press Reload.
strings.settings.display.ditherNote: Adds one 8-bit step of triangular noise before the canvas is drawn at the display's 8 bits, so smooth gradients in the half-float frame do not band. Off draws the managed values exactly.
strings.settings.display.scopeNote: Colour management applies to the photograph — the canvas, the navigator and the filmstrip. The interface itself is never managed, so its greys are the Mac's.
strings.settings.rendering.previewReason: The Windows preview develops each photo at its own resolution; there is no separate interactive resolution to choose yet.
strings.settings.rendering.fastStockReason: Windows has no print-stock preview table yet: a paper change reprints the frame.
strings.settings.rendering.blueCompensationReaso: The Windows engine does not have the Digital Intermediate's blue compensation yet.
strings.settings.rendering.cropRemapsReason: On Windows a crop never changes the film's physical scale yet: grain, halation and glare stay those of the whole frame, the Mac's default.
strings.settings.rendering.decoupleReason: Windows always shows each film effect's strength beside its switch (Film Format, on the Parameters rail), so there is nothing to switch.
strings.settings.memory.title: Memory
strings.settings.memory.reason: The Windows engine does not report its memory or take a reserve and a cap yet, so there is nothing here to read or set.
strings.settings.diskCache.title: Disk cache
strings.settings.diskCache.reason: The Windows app keeps no disk cache of decodes and prints yet; a photo is decoded again when it is reopened.
strings.settings.diagnostics.filesNote: Where this session keeps its preferences and each photo's settings. A run started with --edit-store or --settings-file keeps them where it was told to.
strings.settings.diagnostics.title: Diagnostics
strings.settings.diagnostics.jobLog: Write a job log beside exports
strings.settings.diagnostics.reason: This Windows build keeps no session log: diagnostics go to the console (standard error), and SPEKTRALAB_COLOR_LOG=1 adds every colour management decision.
strings.settings.logs.title: Logs
strings.settings.bundle.title: Diagnostic bundle
strings.settings.bundle.reason: The diagnostic bundle collects the session logs, which the Windows build does not write yet.
strings.settings.agents.toggle: Allow command line and agent access
strings.settings.agents.reason: The spektralab command and the MCP server for agents are part of the macOS app; the Windows build has neither yet.
strings.about.title: About SpektraLab
strings.about.tagline: A spectral film and print simulation for Windows.
strings.about.usesSpektrafilm: SpektraLab uses the spektrafilm engine, film and paper profiles, and the print-preview LUTs baked from them.
strings.about.credit.science: Film simulation, measured profiles and print model
strings.about.credit.monochromeLine: Hanze Qiu — the four measured black-and-white film profiles, SpektraLab's own data (the notice below says what each is built from)
strings.about.credit.appLine: Free software under the GNU GPL v3 or later. You have the right to the corresponding source.
strings.about.lutNote: The print-preview LUTs are derivatives of the profiles and carry the same CC BY-SA 4.0 licence.
strings.about.licence.gpl: GNU GPL v3 — the application and the engine
strings.about.licence.profiles: CC BY-SA 4.0 — the spektrafilm profiles and the print LUTs
strings.about.licence.librawLgpl: GNU LGPL 2.1 — LibRaw, the RAW decoder
strings.about.licence.qt: GNU LGPL v3 — Qt, with its bills of materials
strings.about.licence.texGyre: GUST Font License — TeX Gyre Heros, the film edge's type
strings.about.licence.thirdParty: Third-party notes for this Windows build
strings.about.licenceMissing: {0} is missing from this build's licenses folder. Build with build-msvc.ps1, which deploys it.
strings.about.showLicenceFiles: Show the licence files in Explorer
strings.dialog.import.title: Import One or More RAW Photos
strings.postDev.tabHelp: Post-Dev: the grade on the finished print — white balance, exposure, curves, colour balance and vignetting. It never changes the film or the paper.
strings.postDev.noPhoto: Open a photograph to grade it.
strings.postDev.bypassed: Adjustments bypassed — the canvas and every export show the print without Post-Dev. Ctrl+Shift+B restores them.
strings.postDev.whiteBalanceScope: Print — an adjustment on the scan.
strings.postDev.resetExposure: Reset exposure, contrast, brightness, saturation, highlights, shadows and the black and white points
strings.postDev.vignettingNote: Lens fall-off on the print (Post-Dev), about the centre of the whole frame before the crop -- with Film Edge, of the whole film. Negative darkens the corners.
strings.navigator.title: Navigator
strings.clipboard.title: Settings Clipboard
strings.clipboard.syncReason: Open a photo and select the photos to sync its settings to in the filmstrip.
strings.film.title: Film
strings.film.reset: Reset the film stock to Portra 400
strings.filmEdge.title: Film Edge
strings.filmEdge.toggleHelp: Print the film around the picture: rebate, holes and edge print
strings.filmEdge.switchOn: Switch Film Edge on in its header.
strings.filmEdge.enterPairHelp: This photograph becomes the first frame of a half-frame pair: two half frames on one piece of film. Add the second with the + on the empty hole.
strings.filmEdge.pairFormat: A half-frame pair is always 135 half, exposed twice on one piece of film.
strings.filmEdge.framing.help: Move the picture under the gate with the crop tool. Return develops; Esc puts it back.
strings.filmEdge.gateUpright: The gate is upright — click for across
strings.filmEdge.gateAcross: The gate is across — click for upright
strings.filmEdge.size:
{0} in a film of about {1}
{2} MP · the border takes no picture pixels
strings.filmEdge.sizeMeasured:
{0} in a film of {1}
{2} MP · the border takes no picture pixels
strings.filmEdge.carrier.help: What a strip scan shows past the film's long edges: nothing, a black carrier or the scan's light
strings.filmEdge.carrier.reason: Only a strip scan reaches past the film's edges.
strings.filmEdge.anotherHelp: Another camera body: a new gate, new margins and new holes
strings.filmEdge.anotherFrameHelp: Another frame of the same roll: a new advance and a new scan
strings.filmEdge.lensExif: Lens f/{0}, from EXIF: the gate's softness.
strings.filmEdge.lensAssumed: Lens f/5.6, assumed: EXIF has no aperture. It sets the gate's softness.
strings.dateBack.title: Date Back
strings.dateBack.toggleHelp: Expose the date onto the negative, as a camera's date back did
strings.dateBack.switchOn: Switch Date Back on in its header.
strings.dateBack.orderHelp: The order the date is written in
strings.dateBack.source.help: Print the shooting date from the RAW, or a date you type
strings.dateBack.typedHelp: The line to print, as you type it: up to 32 characters. Return applies it.
strings.dateBack.withDataWhere: beside the frame, with the date
strings.dateBack.withDataHelp: Print the shooting data beside the frame as well as the date
strings.dateBack.marginNote: On 120 the date prints in the film margin beside the frame.
strings.dateBack.turned: It turned for this frame, so the date runs down the picture.
strings.dateBack.level: It was held level, so the date runs along the picture.
strings.dateBack.noCamera: Film Format is no camera with a date back: 135, half frame or 645 has one; other 120 formats need Film Edge.
strings.dateBack.panoramic: No date back on the panoramic formats.
strings.dateBack.dataNeedsEdge120: A 120 back prints beside the frame, on the film edge: it needs Film Edge.
strings.dateBack.dataNeedsEdge: Data prints beside the frame, on the film edge: it needs Film Edge.
strings.print.title: Print
strings.print.slideScannedDirectly: A slide film is scanned directly, without a paper.
strings.print.reason.positiveFilm: A slide film is already a positive — there is nothing for a paper to interpret. Choose a negative film to print onto paper.
strings.print.reason.silverPaper: A black-and-white paper. Choose a black-and-white film to print on it.
strings.print.reason.colourPaper: A colour paper. A black-and-white film prints on a black-and-white paper.
strings.print.reason.effectsScanFilm: Print effects belong to the print; No Print Profile scans the film without one.
strings.print.reason.edrWindows: Windows shows and writes SDR output; Extended Dynamic Range print profiles need an HDR output path.
strings.print.noneHelp: Scan the developed film instead of printing it — a slide film reads as a positive, a negative film as the negative it is.
strings.print.effectsHelp: Glare and pre-flash. Off leaves the paper's colour transformation and nothing else; their settings are kept.
strings.print.edrScope: Changes the render — canvas, proof and file alike
strings.print.fastFlip: Fast flip (baked LUT, no glare, ignores your print grade)
strings.crop.title: Crop
strings.crop.dragToCrop: Drag on the Picture to Crop
strings.crop.editingNote: Drag the grips or the frame on the unrotated original, or draw a new rectangle outside it (Alt-drag inside); Ctrl-drag along a horizon to straighten. Orientation and straightening return when you finish. Enter confirms, Esc cancels.
strings.crop.sharedNote: Preview and export use the same crop and orientation; the original RAW is never changed.
strings.crop.waitForEditor: Finish or cancel the crop on the canvas first (Enter / Esc).
strings.crop.heldReason: Film Edge frames the picture in its gate. Switch it off to crop.
strings.crop.straightenNote: Straightening applies when you release the slider. The edges tighten automatically so no blank corners show.
strings.enlarger.title: Enlarger
strings.enlarger.reset: Reset the enlarger to the solved pack
strings.enlarger.reason.slide: A slide film is scanned directly; there is no print to expose or filter.
strings.toolbar.undoHelp: Undo the last adjustment to this photo · Ctrl+Z
strings.toolbar.redoHelp: Redo the adjustment to this photo · Ctrl+Shift+Z / Ctrl+Y
strings.toolbar.cropHelp: Crop — drag the grips or move the frame; drag outside it (or Alt-drag) to draw a new one; Ctrl-drag a line to straighten
strings.toolbar.processHelp: Auto-exposure and the enlarger filter pack for this paper — print this frame.
strings.toolbar.processUnavailable: Process needs a developed photo and nothing else in progress.
strings.toolbar.processed: Solved · filter pack C {0} · M {1} · Y {2}
strings.toolbar.originalHelp: Show the RAW as decoded, before any film simulation (Space does the same while held)
strings.toolbar.originalShowingHelp: Showing the original — click to go back to the developed print
strings.toolbar.proofHelp: Soft proof (S): show the canvas as the export recipe's colour space ({0}) will render it
strings.toolbar.proofUnavailable: The recipe writes a Digital Intermediate, which has no colour space to proof
strings.toolbar.gamutWarningHelp: Gamut warning (Shift+S): mark in magenta the colours {0} cannot hold
strings.toolbar.zoomFitted: Fitted to the window — {0} % (Ctrl+0). Click for the zoom menu.
strings.toolbar.zoomAt: Zoom — {0} %. Click for the zoom menu; Ctrl+wheel zooms about the pointer.
strings.toolbar.zoomActual: 100 % — one screen pixel per photo pixel (Ctrl+1). Click to fit; right-click for the zoom menu.
strings.canvas.emptyHint: Import RAW photos and choose a film and paper for each
strings.strip.syncHelp: Apply this photo's film, paper, decode and effects to the selected photos. The crop is not synced.
strings.strip.selectHelp: Include in the selection that Sync and batch export use (Ctrl+click)
strings.strip.empty: Drop RAW photos here, or press Ctrl+O.
strings.pair.title: Half-Frame Pair
strings.pair.spacingOnStrip: With Film Edge on, the camera's advance sets the gap.
strings.pair.filmNote: Click a frame on the canvas to pick it; right-click it to replace or crop it.
strings.pair.scopeHelp: Frame: this frame alone. + Film: the film around it -- the gap, the rebate, the edge print -- moves by the same amount.
strings.pair.frameNote: Its metering, exposure and white balance are in Input / Camera on the right, its grade in Post-Dev; its print in Enlarger.
strings.pair.emptyNote: An empty hole is unexposed film. Fill both to export the pair.
strings.pair.noCrop: A half-frame pair has no crop: each frame is placed under its hole.
strings.pair.noCandidates: No photographs in this folder's filmstrip.
strings.pair.addFrameHelp: Put a frame in this hole
strings.pair.cropHint: Drag to move the picture · scroll to scale
strings.pair.menu.turnCamera: Turn the Camera (One Above the Other)
strings.pair.menu.holdLevel: Hold the Camera Level (Side by Side)
strings.latitude.title: Latitude
strings.latitude.empty: Develop the frame to measure it against this film and paper.
strings.latitude.unmeasurable: This film and paper do not print a rising tone scale, so there is no latitude to measure. A slide printed onto print film comes out as a negative.
strings.latitude.noLight: The frame has no light in it to measure.
strings.latitude.plotHelp: The frame on the stop axis from the metered mid-grey, after Scene Placement. The dashed lines are the film and paper's ISO 6846 boundaries; the band under the plot is the chain's tonal separation per stop.
strings.camera.title: Input / Camera
strings.camera.filmExposureNote: Where the scene sits on the film's curve, in stops: grain, latitude and saturation move; the print is re-timed to it. Each photo's settings save automatically.
strings.camera.pickNeutral: Pick a neutral point on the image
strings.camera.pickNeutralHint: Click a neutral grey or white in the picture · Esc cancels
strings.camera.pickNeutralDone: White balance set from the picked point: {0} K, tint {1}
strings.camera.pickNeutralUnavailable: Open a RAW photo, and wait for the current operation, to pick a neutral point.
strings.camera.reasonDecodeWB: Decode white balance applies to RAW input only.
strings.camera.reasonNoMatrix: LibRaw has no colour matrix for this camera, so its white balance can't be changed.
strings.camera.reasonNoAsShot: This RAW records no camera white balance to pin to.
strings.camera.temperatureHelp: Decode white balance in kelvin; the tick is the camera's As Shot value. Changing it re-decodes the RAW.
strings.camera.tintHelp: Decode white balance, green (−) to magenta (+); the tick is the camera's As Shot value.
strings.camera.asShotFilmExposureHelp: Ticked when the frame is exposed exactly as the camera recorded it: metering Custom and no compensation. Ticking it sets both.
strings.camera.meteredHelp: The meter's reading for this frame ({0}); Film Exposure is an offset from it.
strings.camera.vignettingReason: Vignetting is part of the post-development grade (the Mac's Layer 2 lens fall-off), which comes to Windows with the Post-Dev adjustments.
strings.camera.lensCorrectionReason: The Windows RAW decode (LibRaw) has no lens profiles, so there is no lens correction to apply.
strings.format.title: Film Format
strings.format.note: The physical format's long edge sets the scale of grain and halation; cropping does not change the format.
strings.format.reset: Reset the film format and its effects
strings.format.resetStrengths: Reset effect strengths to the film's own
strings.effect.highlightBoostNote: Stops added to the highlights before the halo is drawn, standing in for the energy a clipped RAW no longer holds. 0 is off.
strings.effect.reasonOff: Turn the effect on to set its strength.
strings.effect.reasonHalationOff: Turn Halation on to set this.
strings.effect.reasonPrintEffectsOff: Print Effects is off in the Print section.
strings.placement.title: Scene Placement
strings.placement.reasonMeasuring: Waiting for the latitude measurement of the current settings.
strings.placement.highlightHelp: Stops the scene's top is drawn in toward the medium before the film sees it. The band on the track is what the fit can take.
strings.placement.shadowHelp: Stops the scene's bottom is drawn in toward the medium before the film sees it. The band on the track is what the fit can take.
strings.mask.title: Tone Mask
strings.mask.caption: Change in paper exposure against the blurred negative, stops
strings.mask.reasonPrintEffectsOff: Print Effects is off in the Print section.
strings.mask.reasonInactive: Enable the Tone Mask to set it.
strings.decode.title: RAW Decode
strings.decode.compatibleNote: Matches the validated native RAW pipeline.
strings.decode.headroomNote: Keeps some highlights and negative values after demosaicing; demosaicing is still integer.
strings.info.title: Photo Info
strings.status.title: Status
strings.status.closing: Closing once the current operation finishes…
strings.placeholder.process: Process — auto-exposure and the enlarger filter pack for this paper — is coming to Windows.
strings.placeholder.original: Showing the original RAW before the film simulation is coming to Windows.
strings.placeholder.compare: The before / after split is coming to Windows.
strings.placeholder.latitude: The latitude graph — the scene in stops against this film and paper — is coming to Windows.
strings.placeholder.asShot: Film exposure as shot is coming to Windows.
strings.placeholder.whiteBalance: Decode white balance is coming to the Windows RAW decode.
strings.placeholder.lensCorrection: Lens correction is coming to the Windows RAW decode.
strings.placeholder.scenePlacement: Scene Placement is coming to Windows.
strings.placeholder.toneMask: The Tone Mask is coming to Windows.
strings.placeholder.digitalIntermediate: The Digital Intermediate — the negative with its orange mask removed and reversed on the film's own neutral curve, as Cineon log — needs a Cineon view of the canvas, which is coming to Windows.
strings.placeholder.clipboard: Copying and pasting chosen groups of settings is coming to Windows; Sync copies this photo's settings now.
strings.export.title: Export
strings.export.format.title: Format and Size
strings.export.depth.help: Bit depth. 16-bit switches to TIFF, 8-bit to PNG.
strings.export.depth.fixed: {0} has one depth — it is part of the format.
strings.export.di.what: The frame's Digital Intermediate, whatever paper is chosen: the negative with its orange mask removed, as 16-bit Cineon log in the session's working primaries, untagged.
strings.export.di.next: Next: open it in Resolve, Nuke or Photoshop with one of the two view LUTs beside it (to ProPhoto RGB, to Rec.709) — the view the canvas shows.
strings.export.colorSpace.help: The space the file is converted to, once, through the engine's gamut mapping, and tagged with.
strings.export.preview.help: Writes a preview image into the TIFF, about a tenth larger. Off unless a recipe asks for it.
strings.export.size.help: Original keeps each frame's own pixels. Long edge resamples every frame so its longer side is the number you set, whichever way round the frame is.
strings.export.size.edgeHelp: Pixels on the longer side, 16–60000. Frames are never enlarged.
strings.export.size.batchOriginal: {0} for this frame · {1} more at their own sizes
strings.export.size.batchLongEdge: {0} for this frame · {1} more, each keeping its own shape, none enlarged
strings.export.openWith.help: Hand the finished files to this application when the export ends.
strings.export.formula.title: Export Formula
strings.export.formula.lastRecipe: The last recipe cannot be deleted
strings.export.formula.renameNote: The name in the recipe list.
strings.export.location.title: Location
strings.export.location.chooseTitle: Where Should This Recipe Write Its Files?
strings.export.location.besideHelp: Each frame's own folder. A batch drawn from several folders therefore writes into several — the line below counts them.
strings.export.location.fixedHelp: One folder for every frame in the batch.
strings.export.location.existingHelp: What to do when a file of that name is already there. Nothing is ever replaced unless this says Overwrite.
strings.export.location.manyFolders: {0} folders — one beside each original, starting {1}
strings.export.naming.title: Naming
strings.export.naming.lastPart: A filename needs at least one part
strings.export.metadata.title: Metadata
strings.export.metadata.exifHelp: Carry the camera's shooting data into the file. Orientation is always upright.
strings.export.summary.title: Summary
strings.export.nothingOpen: No frame is open. Choose one from the strip.
strings.export.worklistEmpty: Nothing is selected. Select photos in the filmstrip to add them.
strings.export.proof.caption: Output preview · {0}
strings.export.proof.di: The file holds Cineon codes; this is the print.
strings.status.ready: Ready · open a RAW file to begin
strings.status.opening: Decoding and rendering the RAW file…
strings.status.previewCurrent: Preview already shows the current settings
strings.status.batchFinished: Batch export finished: {0} exported, {1} skipped (file exists), {2} failed
strings.status.batchCancelled: Batch export cancelled: {0} exported, {1} skipped (file exists), {2} failed
strings.status.syncedKeepingCrops: Photos synced: {0} (each keeps its own crop).

strings.status.redone: Redid the adjustment to this photo
strings.status.pairMade: Half-frame pair made: click a frame to pick it.
strings.status.pairAddSecond: Half-frame pair: add the second frame with the + on the empty hole.
strings.saved.unsaved: Some settings are not saved; see the warning below
strings.saved.automatic: Adjustments save automatically and return when the photo is reopened
